title.en: An Act Enhancing the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act, Amending for the Purpose Republic Act No. 10931 and Appropriating Funds Therefor

text.en:
Section 4 of the same Act is hereby amended to read as follows:
"SEC. 4. Free Higher Education in SUCs and LUCs. - All Filipino students who are either currently enrolled at the time of the effectivity of this Act, or shall enroll at any time thereafter, in courses in pursuance of a bachelor's degree, certificate degree, or any comparable undergraduate degree in any SUC or LUC shall be exempt from paying tuition and other school fees for units enrolled in: Provided, That they pass the entrance examination and other admission and retention requirements of the SUCs and LUCs shall create a mechanism to enable students in the SUC and LUC to voluntarily opt out of the tuition and other school fees subsidy or make a contribution to the school. SUCs and LUCs shall report the tuition payments and contributions collected from these students to the CHED: Provided, further , That the amount required to implement the free tuition and other school fees in SUCs and LUCs shall be determined by the their respective governing boards of SUCs and LUCs based on the projected number of enrollees for each academic year, using the most recent available data on secondary education completion rates provided by the Department of Education (DepEd), and projected enrollment data of SUCs and LUCs, which shall be reviewed and validated by the CHED prior to its use as the primary factor in computing the annual proposed budget of SUCs and, in the case of LUCs, the CHED for such purpose, and shall in turn serve as the baseline during the preparation of the annual National Expenditure Program (NEP) by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM): Provided, finally, That the UniFAST Board shall accurately project enrollment rates and the corresponding budget requirements to ensure sufficiency of allocated resources."

A new Section 5-A is hereby inserted to read as follows:
"SEC. 5-A. Equity in Participation in SUCs, LUCs, and State-Run TVIs. - To promote equity in access to quality tertiary education, all SUCs, LUCs, and state-run TVIs shall develop, publicly disclose, and implement an equity and inclusion plan (EIP) outlining the specific targets and measures adopted to support learners from disadvantaged backgrounds in accessing and completing tertiary education;
Such measures may include, but are not limited to: (a) provision of assistive devices and technologies during the admission process; (b) priority allocation of available housing or dormitory facilities; (c) waiver of admission examination fees; and (d) consideration of an applicant's contextual factors in admission evaluation, which shall be documented and without prejudice to institutional academic freedom, merit-based admission standards, and program-specific requirements.
The CHED and TESDA, in consultation with the UniFAST Board, shall issue implementing guidelines for EIPs, which may be differentiated by institution type, program, and geographic context. These guidelines shall be reviewed at least every four (4) years, taking into account enrollment data, equity outcomes, and institutional capacity."

A new Section 7-A is hereby inserted to read as follows:
"SEC. 7-A. Determination of TES Amounts and Periodic Review. - In determining the appropriate amounts of TES grants under Section 7 hereof, the following UniFAST Board shall be guided by the following:
(a) For students in SUCs, LUCs, and state-run TVIs, the TES may cover all subsidies and allowances, ecept TOSF, which are already free under this Act.
(b) For students in CHED-recognized private HEIs and TESDA-registered private TVIs, the TES may cover all subsidies and allowances, including TOSF;
(c) Once awarded, the TES amount granted to a qualified continuing beneficiary shall not be reduced
(d) Higher TFS amounts may be provided for students enrolled in priority programs jointly identified by the CHED, TESDA, Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev), DSWD, and DepEd;
The UniFAST Board, in coordination with the CHEd and TESDA, shall prioritize the allocation of funds under the national budget for the TES over other scholarship and education assistance programs. For this purpose, the TES shall be fully funded, based on normative costing for qualified poor students, with priority given to beneficiaries of the 4Ps, to enable them to complete their tertiary education program within the prescribed period.
The UniFAST Board shall review and adjust TES amounts every two (2) years, in consultation with the CHED, TESDA, and DBM, to account for inflation and changes in education costs."

A new Section 7-B is hereby inserted to read as follows:
"SEC. 7-B. Private Education Assistance (PEA). - To uphold complementarity between public and private education, and to enable disadvantaged students to enroll in priority programs in CHED-recognized private HEIs and TESDA-registered TVIs, there shall be established a private education assistance (PEA).
The PEA shall be governed by the following parameters:
(a) Student Eligibility - The assistance shall be targeted toward poor and deserving students, as determined by the UniFAST Board. The PEA shall be awarded to applicants based on the ranking of their household per capita income, using th most recent available data from the official poverty assessment system adopted by the National Government or other verifiable proof of income as may be determined by the UniFAST Board: Provided, That said students are enrolled in programs identified as priority by the CHED allocate funds by considering the regions with greatest need for such graduates, vis-a-vis available programs offered predominantly by private HEIs and TVIs: Provided, further , That the UniFAST Board shall also ensure that this assistance complements the TES under Section 7 of this Act, by addressing the eligibility of student who may not be covered by existing grants;
(b) Qualifications of Private HEIs and TEVIs - To qualify for the PEA program, the private HEIs and TVIs shall meet the quality standards prescribed by the UniFAST Board including, but not limited to, program accreditation levels, performance in licensure examinations, school facilities, and other quality assurance mechanisms;
(c) Amount of Assistance - The UniFAST Board shall commission a study to determine the normative cost of learning of tertiary education in CHED-recognized private HEIs and TESDA-registered private TVIs. This study shall serve as the basis for setting the nominal value of the PEA, which shall be subject to review every two (2) years to account for inflation and changes in education costs; and
(d) Pilot Implementation - Upon the effectivity of this Act, the UniFAST Board, through the CHED and TESDA, shall conduct a pilot implementation of the PEA for a period of not more than three (3) years prior to full-scale implementation, subject to availability of funds."

A new Section 10-A is hereby inserted to read as follows:
"SEC. 10-A. Grievance Mechanism. - A grievance committee shall be established within the CHEd and TESDA to investigate and resolve complaints or disputes raised by learners in relation to the implementation of this Act within their respective jurisdictions. Each grievance committee shall include representation from the UniFAST Board.
The UniFAST Board, in coordination with the CHED and TESDA, shall promulgate the necessary guidelines, implement the grievance mechanism, and ensure that updated information on the committees, including their procedures, timelines, and available remedies, is publicly accessible."

Section 13 of the same Act is hereby amended to read as follows:
"SEC. 13. Expansion of the UniFAST Board. - x x x The UniFAST Board shall exercise policy formulation, program harmonization, and monitoring and evaluation functions in relation to student financial assistance programs. The implementation and delivery of such programs shall be undertaken by the appropriate implementing agencies, including the CHED and TESDA, in accordance with their respective mandates.
The UniFAST Board is authorized to establish an enhanced organizational structure, staff development and incentives, and such other administrative measures needed for the efficient discharge of tasks and commensurate to the level and scope of its responsibilities. It may tap the expertise and management services of eligible service providers subject to the appropriate guidelines promulgated by the UniFAST Board."

Appropriations. - The amounts necessary to carry out the provisions of this Act shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act and appropriated under the SUCs, CHED, and TESDA in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

Implementing Rules and Regulations. - Within sixty (60) days from the effectivity of this Act, the implementing rules and regulations (IRR) necessary for the effective and efficient enforcement of this Act shall be formulated, promulgated, and implemented by the UniFAST Board, in consultation with the CHED, TESDA, DepEd, DSWD, DBM, and other relevant stakeholders in higher and technical-vocational education: Provided, That the failure of the Board to promulgate the said rules and regulations shall not prevent or delay the effectivity and implementation of this Act.
Separability Clause. - If any portion or provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional, the remainder thereof or any provision not affected thereby shall remain in force and effect.

Repealing Clause. - All laws, presidential decrees or issuances, executive orders, letters of instruction, or rules and regulations inconsistent with the provisions of this Act are hereby repealed or modified accordingly.

Effectivity. - Notwithstanding the non-issuance of the IRR, this Act shall take effect after fifteen (15) days following its complete publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
